flags.message: Post/footer count: proposal (8) posts with 8 footers governs per canon, but the presentation p.3 plan draws only 7 '6X6 POST' footing symbols at ~7' c/c along a 41'-9" line. If the field layout is 7, groundwork and post-set effort drop ~12%; sized at 8.

Openings: presentation p.4 tags 7 windows (4×3050DH, 2×5050DH, 1×3036DH) plus a 6568 double door on the house wall, versus the signed proposal 'up to (6) 36x60 windows' and (1) 36x80 door. Proposal governs (set is visualization-only, both larger 5050 units and the double door are outside the allowance); sized at 6+1.

Presentation renders show a railed deck, exterior stairs to grade, brick-wrapped posts (Option 1, $0.00) and Option-2-level interior finishes (plank floor, baseboard, painted ceiling, recessed cans) — none in the $66,200 contract. Proposal governs per canon; none of this is sized. Also, no egress from the elevated room is described anywhere.

House-side wall is the existing brick house wall ('Drywall over brick', presentation p.4). Proposal never mentions it; JBD prices 344 sf of drywall there but no furring, fastening, or insulation strategy for masonry — drywall on that wall is under-sized until a furring method is settled.

Ceiling finish is unaddressed: existing ceiling assemblies are demolished, proposal drywall is 'on walls' only, JBD says 'no ceiling drywall', yet renders show a finished painted ceiling. Sized with no ceiling work; if the PM adds ceiling drywall/insulation the drywall bucket grows ~430 sf (+50%).

JBD 455 labor-hours reads hot against the physical takeoff: 65h drywall for 30 sheets (~2.2 h/sheet all-in), 87h floor system for 430 sf, 48h demo for a 430 sf room, 69h walls for 63 LF. Elevated/choppy work justifies some premium, but sizing should anchor to takeoff quantities and the rate card, citing the JBD only as a ceiling.

JBD double-counts WRB labor (6h sheathing+WRB line plus a separate 3h WRB line) and double-prices the 3 dump runs (material $1,350 and equipment $1,350); the hours-side duplication (3h) should not be inherited.

JBD carries zero hours for permits and inspections although the proposal price 'includes permitting' and IRC 2018/NEC compliance; canon expects ~2h per inspection visit — add ~5 visits (footing, framing, electrical rough, mechanical, insulation/final) outside the JBD totals.

'Cut Concrete footers approx. 12x12x12 near existing pad' is ambiguous: cutting into the existing slab would add saw-cut/breakout effort (rate card 1.5h per ~10 sf) and equipment the JBD does not price; sized as hand-dug/bag-mix footers beside the pad.

Wall height (8 ft) and post height (~10 ft) come only from the JBD, not the proposal or drawings; the retained shed roof fixes the wall height and the sloped lot means post lengths vary — field measurement should confirm before framing package order.

All allowance selections (siding profile/color, 6 windows, door, mini-split BTU/location, fixtures) are unmade and no lead times are stated; canon forbids scheduling before final selections and demo cannot start without next-phase materials on site — the 2027-03-01 start assumes selections close well ahead.

Several JBD sections straddle sequence components (floor_system covers framing + soffit cladding + floor batt; excavation_foundation covers footers + posts/beam; roof integration is part framing, part flashing). Splits above are by the JBD's own line-item hours, not equal halves.

Subpanel conversion is contingent on the existing fused disconnect being sound and legally usable as a subpanel (JBD PM note); a replacement subpanel would be an add. Main service is 200A per project answer, so capacity is not the concern — panel condition is.
